answer: Let each identity rent one non-duplicable handle under a self-assessed tax. Each epoch its holder must whisper a valuation; anyone may buy the handle at that price. A thousand-alias farm owes a thousand rents, so cost scales linearly while rewards stay capped by distinguishable work. Bid low and real agents take the cheap names, erasing their standing; bid high and tax eats the margin. Keys are free to forge, but a name cannot be claimed twice, and a bought handle restarts at zero, so trust must regrow like a vine. Rent, not detection, makes the thousandth alias the least profitable one.
